clue.text: Beastly accommodation

parts.note: read 'beastly' as 'for beasts' rather than 'nasty': housing for horses and other animals

explanation.surface: A complaint about dreadful lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like a grumble about poor rooms; read literally it means for animals, and the buildings that house horses are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stables are buildings where horses and other livestock are kept, so they are lodging for beasts.

clue.text: Staid they may be aboard, but perverse

annotationWithheld.why: Staid they may be aboard, but perverse (7): STAID anagrammed inside SS, but 'aboard' must be both the container indicator and the SS letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Staid they may be aboard, but perverse

clue.text: Heats and cools gradually Ann's bitter concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed up, so the letters of the woman's name and the beer are stirred together

parts.note: the possessive gives ANNS, letters as written
bitter is a type of British beer, an ale

explanation.surface: Ann brews a bitter drink by heating and cooling it slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' mixes ANNS with ALE (bitter, a British beer) to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalworkers and glassmakers treat material this way, warming then slowly chilling it to toughen it.

clue.text: Reasonable chain of thought

parts.note: a sequence of reasoning that holds together, the discipline of sound argument

explanation.surface: A description of a sensible line of reasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the study and practice of valid reasoning, the sound linking of one step of thinking to the next.

clue.text: In which a Q.C. keeps his small change?

definitions.text: In which a Q.C. keeps his small change?

parts.words: In which a Q.C. keeps his small change?
parts.note: a Queen's Counsel is called a 'silk' from the silk gown worn, so the barrister's coin holder is pictured as one made of silk

explanation.surface: Asking where a senior barrister keeps loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: A Q.C. (Queen's Counsel, a senior British barrister) is known as a silk; the phrase also recalls the proverb about not making one from a sow's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bag for coins made of the fabric that names senior barristers.

clue.text: Spanish nobleman in a state in Mexico

definitions.meaning: a member of the minor Spanish gentry
a central Mexican state whose capital is Pachuca

explanation.surface: A Spanish grandee found living in a Mexican region.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a Spanish gentleman of lower nobility and is also the name of a Mexican state.

clue.text: Gets touchy over draughts?

definitions.meaning: in the board game draughts (checkers), removing an opponent's piece that failed to capture is called this

explanation.surface: Someone gets irritable about cold air blowing in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draughts' suggests chilly air; it is the board game, in which a piece forfeited for not capturing is taken this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulking in a temper, and the old penalty move in draughts that removes a piece, share this word.

clue.text: Time for steady diversion from work

indicators.note: a diversion sends things off their usual path, so these letters are rerouted into a new order

explanation.surface: A call for steady leisure away from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion from work' rearranges the letters of 'for steady'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday or other day off is a period set aside for leisure, a span of time.

clue.text: The smallest round Wearside make the most spare

indicators.note: round means the following word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: the smallest amount is the least
Wearside, around Sunderland on the River Wear, is in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Sunderland's tiniest folk prove the thinnest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts NE inside LEAST. Wearside is the Sunderland area in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean thin or lean, so the thinnest of all is the superlative.

clue.text: Venue for those who want to go out to play

definitions.text: Venue for those who want to go out to play

parts.words: Venue for those who want to go out to play
parts.note: read 'go out to play' as attending a stage performance held outdoors, not children going out

explanation.surface: Somewhere for those who fancy playing outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go out to play' sounds like children heading outdoors; read it as going to see a play staged in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage without a roof where drama is performed outdoors is a place to see plays outside.

clue.text: Irish county to make one glad

indicators.note: make here means remake or form into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish county that is said to cheer a person up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the letters of 'one glad'. Donegal is a county in the far north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in Ulster.

clue.text: Mixed by an elf it's deadly to an insect

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of the words that follow are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: An elf blends a poison that kills insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' rearranges the letters of 'by an elf'.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant name describes something that poisons the common insect pest, as wolfsbane harms wolves.

clue.text: Water-colours in the main not Landseer's forte, possibly

definitions.text: Water-colours in the main not Landseer's forte, possibly

parts.words: Water-colours in the main not Landseer's forte, possibly
parts.note: 'the main' is the sea, so these are paintings of the ocean, unlike the animal pictures for which Landseer was famous

explanation.surface: An art critic remarks that Landseer was not mainly a watercolourist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water-colours' suggests the painting medium and 'in the main' suggests 'mostly'; read them as pictures of water and 'the main' as the sea. Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintings depicting the ocean are pictures of the sea, which crosswords call the main.

clue.text: She's revolutionary in soccer's ruling body

indicators.note: in means the first piece sits within the second

parts.note: the Football Association, English soccer's governing body, is the FA
a revolutionary, a communist, is a red

explanation.surface: A woman radical sits on the football authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RED inside FA, the Football Association that runs English football.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a girl's name, so it stands for a woman, any 'she'.

clue.text: Hempen form of sails

indicators.note: a form of something is that thing reshaped, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rope fibre made from canvas sails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges the letters of 'sails'. The definition is used as an adjective, the fibre name serving attributively, as in sisal rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre used like hemp for rope and twine.

clue.text: Have fun with a bird nearby

parts.note: a lark is a songbird, the skylark
about can mean around or close at hand

explanation.surface: Enjoy oneself with a feathered friend close by.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool around playfully is to have a merry time.

clue.text: Consider alternatively a throw-back

parts.note: to consider is to reflect
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Thinking again about something old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw-back' suggests something reverting to the past; here it means a thing that throws light back.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror or cat's eye returns light, so it throws it back.

clue.text: Where on earth democracy rules OK?

definitions.text: Where on earth democracy rules OK?

parts.words: Where on earth democracy rules OK?
parts.note: the Cold War term for the non-communist nations, where democratic government prevails, with a nod to graffiti's 'rules OK'

explanation.surface: Asking which corner of the planet democracy dominates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rules OK' is a British graffiti formula ('X rules OK') proclaiming supremacy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the Western name for liberal democratic countries opposed to the Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Replace pure seeds

annotationWithheld.why: Replace pure seeds (9): 'Replace' is both the definition and the only anagram indicator for 'pure seeds'

clue.text: Quiet walk with an awkward gait

definitions.text: Quiet walk with an awkward gait

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
an amble is a leisurely walk

explanation.surface: A gentle stroll taken clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a shuffling walk is a quiet, ungainly one.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle along clumsily is to move with an awkward, dragging step.

clue.text: Ruff to adorn Chanticleer's fabulous mate

definitions.meaning: a sixteenth-century neck covering with a collar or frill
in the fable of the cockerel Chanticleer (Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale), his favourite hen bears this name

explanation.surface: A frilled collar to decorate the cockerel's partner in the tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means from a fable, not wonderful. Chanticleer is the rooster of medieval beast fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old garment covering the neck and the hen who partners the fabled rooster.

clue.text: It's the feet that feel the pinch

definitions.text: It's the feet that feel the pinch

parts.words: It's the feet that feel the pinch
parts.note: 'pinch' means steal; the letters of 'the feet' with one E lost make a word for stealing

explanation.surface: Tight shoes hurt the feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinch' suggests tight shoes; it is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinch, in slang, is an act of stealing.

clue.text: Follow the example of a bird no longer with us

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
the late person is dead

explanation.surface: Copy a bird that has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone admired is to imitate them.

clue.text: See 8
Main arterial way

parts.note: 'arterial way' sounds like a major road; read medically it is the chief artery of the body

explanation.surface: A description of a trunk road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main arterial way' reads as a major road; it is the body's principal artery, leaving the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The great artery leaving the heart is the chief channel for blood.

clue.text: Where one lives when one leaves the country!

definitions.text: Where one lives when one leaves the country!

parts.words: Where one lives when one leaves the country!
parts.note: 'leaves the country' suggests emigrating; it means leaving the countryside for a home in the city

explanation.surface: Asking where an emigrant lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves the country' sounds like going abroad; it means going from a rural estate to a city residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy family's city residence is used when away from their country seat.

clue.text: Large casks one finds in a capital city

indicators.note: 'one finds in' means the numeral sits inside the casks

parts.note: tuns are large casks for wine or beer
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Big barrels discovered in a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds in' places I (one) inside TUNS. Tunis is the capital of Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: Spray water on a prophet

parts.note: to hose is to spray water over something

explanation.surface: Drenching a holy man with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: High-riser appears an all-in blessing

indicators.note: 'all-in' places the word all inside the next piece

parts.note: a boon is a blessing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tall building turns out to be a blessing for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-riser' suggests a tower block; it is something that floats up into the sky. 'in' puts ALL inside BOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas-filled envelope rises high into the air.

clue.text: Give the others a right to begin anew

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Granting everyone else a fresh opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: To start again is to make a fresh beginning.

clue.text: Properties in key areas, say Maryland and Maine

parts.note: E is a musical key
Maryland and Maine are examples of US states

explanation.surface: Land holdings in prime areas of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Large landed possessions are holdings of property.

clue.text: Part of the rig for an expert marksman

definitions.meaning: on a sailing ship, a wooden block with holes through which the lanyards of the shrouds pass

explanation.surface: Someone pairs ship's rigging with a sharpshooter.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a rigging block on sailing ships and also a shooter of deadly accuracy.
